How- ever, cases of acute stent malapposition with a large volume or acute stent malapposition located within the edges of the stent were not resolved in most cases. Thus, acute stent malapposi- by guest on June 16, 2017 tion volume and location within stent edges were identified as independent predictors of late-persistent stent malapposition. Our results indicate that an acute stent malapposition with a larger volume or area is more likely to persist at follow-up examinations, which is consistent with findings from previous studies. 4,6,8 Late-persistent stent malapposition could be differ- entiated from resolved acute stent malapposition by an acute

stent malapposition area >1.2 mm² according to an IVUS study. 6 A strut-to-vessel distance ≤260 µm on poststent OCT images was suggested as a cut-off value for resolved acute stent malapposition. 18 A volume of acute stent malapposition >2.56 mm³ best separated late-persistent stent malapposition lesions from resolved acute stent malapposition lesions in the present study.
